name: R13.1 Answer staff questions from approved sources

nodes.name: Step 1: Staff question
nodes.notes: Your staff chat calls this for each message to the assistant. Body: {message_id, conversation_id, asker, text, reply_to}; asker is the channel's signed-in sender, never anything typed in the message.

assignments.name: hr_phrases
assignments.value: ["<your personal HR phrasings, such as \"my pay\">"]

assignments.name: hr_fixed_reply
assignments.value: <R9.2's fixed reply, naming who to ask>

assignments.name: price_phrases
assignments.value: ["<your price phrasings, such as \"how much is\">"]

assignments.name: price_list_link
assignments.value: https://<your price list in the CRM>

assignments.name: policy_figures
assignments.value: ["<your owner-approved policy figures, such as the meal allowance>"]

assignments.name: relevance_threshold
assignments.value: <your threshold, tuned on last month's questions>

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Edit these values for your company; nothing else in the workflow hard-codes them.

parameters.query: WITH reserved AS (INSERT INTO key_log (recipe, key, status) VALUES ($1, $2, 'in progress') ON CONFLICT (recipe, key) DO NOTHING RETURNING key), skipped AS (UPDATE key_log SET copies_skipped = copies_skipped + 1 WHERE recipe = $1 AND key = $2 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reserved)) SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM reserved) = 1 AS is_new, $2::text AS key

nodes.name: Step 2: Reserve key
nodes.notes: Key log: refuses a second copy in the same step (book Chapter 2).

nodes.name: Duplicate: stop
nodes.notes: This message was answered before.

parameters.query: SELECT (SELECT rules->>'owner' FROM decision_log WHERE recipe = 'R13.1' AND item = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1) AS owner, (SELECT rules->>'topic' FROM decision_log WHERE recipe = 'R13.1' AND item = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1) AS topic

nodes.name: Read the answer's decision log
nodes.notes: Who owns the answer the asker says is wrong.

nodes.name: Step 4: Read the asker's groups
nodes.notes: Read-only directory access.

nodes.name: Step 5: Search current, in-date passages
nodes.notes: The index filters on audience, status and dates inside the query, before ranking.

nodes.name: Read the source register
nodes.notes: Owners, titles and links for each source.

nodes.name: Step 6: Rule: above the relevance threshold?
Step 7: Read live sharing
nodes.notes: Who can open the document now, not the index's stored copy.

nodes.name: Step 7: Rule: drop documents the asker cannot open
Step 8: Build the AI request
nodes.notes: Fills the prompt from the recipe's prompts/ file; the input is data, never instructions.

nodes.name: Step 8: AI call
nodes.notes: Claude Haiku 5.5 by default (Config); tools none; the reply is checked by the rule that follows.

nodes.name: Step 11: Read the source register again
nodes.notes: Read after the AI step, so a source withdrawn since step 5 is caught.

nodes.name: Rules: steps 9 to 12
nodes.notes: The rules decide, not the AI.

nodes.name: Outcome
nodes.notes: Every path's reply and log entry, as Table 13.2 sets them.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ conversation_id: $('Step 1: Staff question').first().json.body.conversation_id, reply_to: $('Step 1: Staff question').first().json.body.message_id, to: $('Step 1: Staff question').first().json.body.asker, text: $('Outcome').item.json.reply }) }}

nodes.name: Steps 12 and 13: Reply to the asker

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ to: $('Config').first().json.hr_contact, subject: 'Personal HR question from ' + $('Step 1: Staff question').first().json.body.asker, text: $('Step 1: Staff question').first().json.body.text }) }}

nodes.name: Step 3: Pass the question to HR

parameters.query: INSERT INTO exception_queue (recipe, item, reason, detail, owner) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5) RETURNING id

nodes.name: Exception queue: gap
nodes.notes: Exception queue: a named person works through it (book Chapters 2 and 16).

INSERT INTO decision_log (recipe, item, decision, rules) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4::jsonb) RETURNING id

nodes.name: Decision log
nodes.notes: Decision log: the item's ID, the decision and the rules; never the content (book Chapter 3).
